contractRules.rule: TypeInfo imports QueryIdentity, SemanticFlightKey, InputBasisId and ResultContractId from verter_identity and CertifiedTypeEngineBinding from verter_session unchanged. It defines no generic key, flight, basis or contract type, no alias of one, and no wrapper that adds a field to one. Its only additions are the per-descriptor query-kind marker Q and the canonical semantic-argument encoding it passes to QueryIdentity::compose.

A native fact's basis is the InputBasisId of the captured view the request resolved against. A TypeScript-authoritative fact's basis is the PublishSnapshot::input_basis its CertifiedTypeEngineBinding certified. A composed result's basis is the ordered list of its children's bases. That list is not an InputBasisId, so it cannot fill SemanticFlightKey.input_basis. The composed result mints no basis and no flight key. Each child keeps the one InputBasisId it was observed under. TypeObservationBasis names this role and is not a new type (TIF-F01).

Execution limits never enter QueryIdentity, ResultContractId or SemanticFlightKey: ExecutionPolicy (deadline, cancellation, priority, work and memory budget) and the SKR-READS BudgetProfile. A budget changes only the identity of a refusal (DEM0 DR19); it can never produce a different value labelled Complete.

Presentation never enters QueryIdentity: display policy, qualification, branding and display budgets are PresentationProfileId. Wire shape never enters it: schema version, string-table layout, graph-export layout and whether already-recorded provenance or diagnostics are serialized are SerializationProfileId. A requester coordinate encoding never enters any identity (ENC0 R08).

TypeScript interpretation (strictness, module resolution, lib, JSX) enters QueryIdentity only as the TypeScriptSemanticProfileId among the observed profiles. Backend, process and provider identity (EngineIdentity, ProviderEpoch, serving lease, reported version) never enter it (VID0 R14); they are value-side provenance of TypeScript-authoritative facts (TR26).

The selector set is closed: Position, FileName, ProjectName, WorkspaceName, Component and NodeRef. Component is FileName plus an export name and a typed FrameworkProfileId; its facets are TIF1D's. NodeRef addresses a node of an earlier result by that result's (QueryIdentity, InputBasisId) and the node's stable decl-slot identity, never by opaque bytes. A selector is decoded into typed identities at the adapter; an undecodable selector is a typed request error before execution.

A Position selector is (SourceUnitId, SourceByteOffset or SourceByteRange in CD1) and always carries a source-revision basis (SourceRevision, ContentId). A position in a generated or embedded domain reaches CD1 only through its map owner, with the MapRevision it was mapped through. A requester encoding is converted once at the adapter (ENC0 R03). A position whose basis is not live is refused as StaleSelector; it is never re-mapped, clamped or snapped (ENC0 R06, R09).

A FileName selector is a SourceUnitId plus a declaration name and namespace (type, value or namespace) or an export name. The adapter decodes a path into a SourceUnitId through the registered source authority; an unknown path is a typed UnknownSource error, never a guessed unit and never a scratch file.

A ProjectName selector is a ConfiguredProjectId plus a module specifier and an export name, resolved through that project's own module resolution. When a request names a source without a project, the owner is the one provider-neutral default-configured-owner decision of the workspace snapshot; a selector never picks the first project that answers.

A WorkspaceName selector is a name across the workspace. The workspace index supplies candidate declarations only; it never answers a type fact and never acts as a checker. Each candidate is answered on demand as its own FileName or ProjectName observation. More than one candidate is Ambiguous { candidates }; nothing picks one.

Every selector carries exactly one basis: SourceRevision (a position, or a name pinned to one revision) or CapturedView (an InputBasisId of a captured project or workspace view). A request may ask for the current view; the host then captures it and reports that InputBasisId in the result. A pinned basis that is no longer live is StaleBasis. An input the basis needs and does not hold is NeedInputs, never treated as absent (CFG0 CR23).

Name matching is exact on the canonical name: no prefix, fuzzy, case-folded or first-match search. Same-name merged declarations are one symbol (the MergedDecl carrier). The same name in two namespaces, or declared by two owners of one file, is Ambiguous unless the selector names the namespace or owner.

The operation descriptor set is closed (OP01-OP12). A new operation is a new descriptor row with its own route, contract and owner. IDE features that are not type information (references, rename, completion, semantic tokens, document highlights, code actions) stay on their LSP provider routes and are not TypeInfo operations.

A descriptor names: the operation kind; the selector kinds it accepts; its semantic arguments (projection mode, reduction demand, closure policy, path, substitutions, type arguments, the canonical encoding of a structured expression); its ResultContractId; the capability cell DEM0 P4 demands (VID0 I10); its route class; and its execution owner. Only arguments that can change the answer are semantic arguments.

Canonical equality material is QueryIdentity::compose(descriptor domain tag, digest of the canonical selector subject plus semantic arguments, the observed profile set, ResultContractId). The basis is not in it. It enters a SemanticFlightKey only when the fact's basis is one InputBasisId (TR28), and it always enters value-side provenance. A composed request's QueryIdentity is TR21; it has no SemanticFlightKey, and its cache scope is TR32. Two requests that differ only in presentation, serialization, execution limits or requester encoding have equal QueryIdentity.

Canonical semantic equality is separate from presentation order. Facts, candidates and members are ordered by canonical encoding (union and intersection arms by VerterStableV1); authored or source order is a presentation projection that changes no equality. The order is the same under any file-load, interning, query or thread schedule.

Every request is validated before any semantic execution, as the typeinfo wire contract already requires. An unknown descriptor, an unknown selector kind, a selector its descriptor does not accept, or an argument outside the descriptor's range is a typed request error.

Each (descriptor, selector kind, region claim) has exactly one route class: Native, TypeScriptAuthoritative or Composed. The route class decides the execution owner; nothing chooses an owner by trying one and falling back to another.

A Native route that answers a fact Verter's engine owns — a declaration lowered to typed IR, a macro payload, or a framework facet — executes only through ProjectSemanticDispatch, the one type-resolution engine. The parentheticals on OP05 (flow substrate) and OP07 (relation oracle) name that engine's substrate; they are the same owner and the same route class. A Native route that answers the shallow symbol inventory (OP08 ListSymbols) reads the IndexedReady artifact through the session and does not issue a ProjectSemanticDispatch query. OP08's one execution owner is that IndexedReady read.

A TypeScriptAuthoritative route executes only through EngineBackend over a CertifiedTypeEngineBinding reached from a BoundProject. The native engine never recreates such a fact. Without a binding the fact is Unavailable { NoProject | ProviderUnavailable | NotReady }, never a native answer.

A Composed route is an ordered list of child observations, each a full observation with its own route class and its own execution owner. The composition owner executes no child. Composition is per fact: each fact keeps the one authority that produced it. Two authorities that answer the same question both appear with their authorities; no field-wise winner is chosen. A composed result's QueryIdentity is composed over the composition descriptor and the child QueryIdentities. The composed result mints no InputBasisId and no SemanticFlightKey (TR02, TR28).

Each (descriptor, selector kind, region claim) has exactly one route class and exactly one execution owner. A Composed region's execution owner is its composition owner; it executes no child. Each child in that plan has exactly one route class and one execution owner: Native through the owner TR19 names, or TypeScriptAuthoritative through EngineBackend (TR20). A region missing that shape is a construction failure of the descriptor table. A route the table names but the host does not serve answers a typed Unsupported refusal; it is never validated and then dropped.

A result carries: the typed selector echo; the descriptor id; the QueryIdentity digest; the basis (TR02), plus required_version, content_hash and map_hash for a TypeScript-authoritative fact; the facts, each with value, authority (Native, TypeScript, Framework { FrameworkProfileId } or Composed), per-fact quality, and provenance (decl-slot identity, SourceUnitId and CD1 range, ReleaseId for framework facts); candidates or ambiguity; any refusal; the reuse class; and the SKR-READS evidence (proof, diagnostic recipes, recovery, cost receipt, footprint). Explanations and traces are optional capture.

Per-fact quality is one of Complete, Approximate { cause } or Unavailable { cause }, and it lives only in result provenance. A request states demand (mode, closure, path), never completeness. A result-level completeness, where shown, is derived from its facts. A cached candidate's nominal mode never claims completeness (CLAUDE.md cache satisfaction is the recorded materialized point).

Quality is independent of reuse eligibility. ReuseClass (Shared, RequestOnly, NoReuse) is reported beside it. A deterministically Approximate fact may be Shared. An eligible refusal is reused only under its exact refusal identity (DEM0 DR19) and stays a refusal; it is never read as exact absence, and an edit invalidates it like any other entry.

Provider identity is provenance, kept apart from the semantic value. No DTO carries a provider handle: no BoundProject, binding, serving lease, session handle, live pointer or opaque bytes that dereference host or provider state.

Ambiguity is a typed outcome: Ambiguous { candidates }, candidates in canonical order, each with its own provenance. Cancellation, budget, stale basis and unsettled input are typed causes. A miss caused by churn or a non-current view is Unavailable { UnsettledInput }, never the same signal as 'no such declaration'.

Candidate lookup is keyed by QueryIdentity. In-flight production of a fact whose basis is one InputBasisId is keyed by SemanticFlightKey (QueryIdentity, that InputBasisId). Both keys belong to the accepted runtime owner (G2 flight law, PER0D). A composed request has no SemanticFlightKey: its basis is the ordered child list (TR02), which is not an InputBasisId, and TypeInfo mints no basis, alias, wrapper or second key to collapse it (TR01). Concurrent composed requests share work only through their children's flights. The composed cache entry is TR32, not a flight. TypeInfo adds no key, no flight, no coalescer and no store; every cache it reads is a ProjectTypeStore cache.

A warm hit requires the value-side ReadSetSignature facts and self roots to validate against the live store view. A TypeScript-authoritative fact also requires its certified basis to be the live published basis (publish_admitted, serving_admitted). A moved backend, provider epoch or required version makes the fact Unavailable { StaleBackend }; it is neither served nor warmed.
A position-derived fact is valid only for the exact ContentId and MapRevision it was computed on (ENC0 R09). A changed map rejects the fact; it is never re-mapped approximately.

Degraded outcomes (Unavailable, Approximate caused by budget or cancellation, superseded, torn view) are ReturnOnly: they never publish entries, reverse-index metadata or persistent artifacts. Required state survives capture off.

A composed cache entry is scoped by the composition descriptor, the child QueryIdentities and each child's basis. It is isolated by profile, by edit and by evaluation context. A composed entry never satisfies a child query, and a child entry never satisfies a composed one.

findings.finding: TypeObservationBasis, named by the charter as an accepted identity, has no type at this head. The accepted basis of a native or TypeScript-authoritative fact is InputBasisId (crates/verter_identity), minted by InputBasis in verter_analysis_inputs and by PublishSnapshot::input_basis for the certified engine. A composed result's basis is the ordered list of its children's bases. That list is not an InputBasisId and forms no SemanticFlightKey; each child flights on its own key, and TypeInfo mints no composition basis and no second key (TR02, TR28). UAO0 revalidates that no downstream node names TypeObservationBasis as a type or fills SemanticFlightKey from a composed list.

EngineBackend::query returns QueryOutcome::{Answered, NoResultVersionMismatch} with no payload; the engine-native answer rides an out-of-band channel the contract does not model. A TypeScriptAuthoritative TypeInfo fact (OP11, OP12) therefore has no typed DTO at this head; TIF1 models it inside TR23 without adding a second backend contract.

resolve_named_symbol picks the dispatch owner with unique_local_type_declaration_owner_in, which returns None on multi-owner ambiguity; the caller then falls back to the ordinary-file owner without reporting the ambiguity. TR12 and TR27 make that an Ambiguous outcome.

The framework-surface normalizers correlate rows by the first member whose name matches (svelte_exec.rs props_fields.iter().find for $bindable members, which synthesises a field when none matches; vue_exec/normalize_slots.rs members.iter().find for slot occurrences). This is inside the D12/D14 component-information population, not a TypeInfo selector; TIF1D's facet schema and TIF1's cutover own it.

The LSP hover merge (crates/verter_lsp/src/type_provider/merge/hover.rs, merge_hover) prepends the provider's type block to Verter's hover content. It is a presentation merge outside TypeInfo, not a field-wise semantic merge. When a hover adopts OP11, the type fact and any framework fact follow TR21.

GraphExactness and FrameworkSurfaceKindSupport are the current quality vocabulary. Proposed TR24 mapping, for TIF1 to confirm against the engine: EXACT_RESOLVED, EXACT_SYMBOLIC and UNRESOLVED_GENERIC are Complete (an open generic is an exact answer); PARTIAL and CYCLE are Approximate; MISS is Unavailable { NotFound } unless the read set proves absence; UNSUPPORTED, BUDGET_EXCEEDED and UNSTABLE are Unavailable with that cause. A facet's UNSUPPORTED is not-applicable for its profile, which TIF1D defines.
